From end states to pathways
Estimated acceptance, agents with memory, and robust road-pricing paths to a low-carbon Norway in 2050
Arshad Akhtar Abbasia · PhD in Transport Modelling for Sustainability Transitions · PhD programme in Logistics
01 · THE PROBLEM

What an equilibrium cannot carry

Norway appraises transport with a national model system that computes an equilibrium for a chosen year. Asked what 2050 looks like under a set of assumptions, it answers carefully. Asked how the country gets there, and which routes fail on the way, it is silent by construction. TØI’s own review says as much: the current models are static and macroscopic, and less suited to dynamic questions [toi1819]. The path to 2050 is governed by what an equilibrium does not carry: a vehicle fleet that turns over slowly, public acceptance that persists or erodes, and debt repaid on a schedule.

Road pricing shows the problem in its sharpest form. It is named among the levers for the next National Transport Plan, where TRANSPLAN’s first deliverable argues the plan must be realistic and goal-directed rather than a wish list [toi2172]; yet the national reform has stalled. Tolls raised NOK 16.8 billion in 2025, about 62% in city packages, against toll-company debt near NOK 78 billion [svv25, dok15]. Every revision meets a public that has voted against tolls before: a single-issue anti-toll party won 16.7% in Bergen in 2019 [snl19]. Whether a 2050 plan is feasible depends on the order in which instruments arrive and whether people accept each step. That is a question about paths.

Main question. Which sequences of road-pricing instruments reach a desirable 2050 on emissions, finance and accessibility while staying acceptable to the people and firms who pay, across deep uncertainty; and which signals tell planners when to switch?
RQ1 · method (A1)How can choice models estimated on real data drive agents that carry state year to year, so strategic end states become pathways?
RQ2 · behaviour (A2)Does acceptance persist once a charge is permanent, and does information move it independently of experience?
RQ3 · planning (A3)Which pathways, for passengers and for freight, are robust; what acceptance margin does each survive; and which signposts give lead time before one fails?

What already exists. I have a working prototype and a first measured result. At the Kristiansund tariff a zero-emission car with a tag pays NOK 19.04 against NOK 27.20, so each electric crossing earns NOK 8.16, or 30%, less [vegamot]. At today’s national share of four electric passings in ten, a crossing already earns about 12% less than in a fossil fleet; in an all-electric fleet it earns 30% less while the debt is unchanged. On the road network, the toll-free Atlantic Ocean Tunnel lets some crossings avoid both stations; Article 1 counts that share ([N1]), so exposure is measured on the network, not assumed uniform.

02 · FIT, GAP AND WHAT IS NEW

A dynamic layer beside the national models

The national system has three parts a candidate must name: NTM6, the national passenger model for trips over 70 km; RTM, the regional passenger model; and the national freight model, Nasjonal godsmodell (NGM), with its commodity-flow matrices and transport-chain costs [toi1819, ngm]. These anchor the National Transport Plan and are trusted for point appraisal. TØI’s forward-looking review recommends not replacing them but building dynamic models alongside them [toi1819]; the institute has begun, with a MATSim-based agent assignment for Greater Oslo, tramodsim, and an activity-based model for Trondheim [tramodsim]. This PhD joins that line rather than importing a method from outside it. It supplies the exploratory, stress-testing layer that sequences instruments across thousands of futures and reports where each sequence fails, so the national models keep producing the appraisal the agencies rely on while this layer supplies the robustness and failure conditions they are not built to give.

The position asks forThis proposal answers with
Desirable futures under deep uncertainty10³ futures, satisficing targets, uncertainty decomposed by source
DCM integrated with ABMChoice models estimated on real survey data drive agents whose acceptance and fleet carry over year to year
Behaviour under low-carbon scenarios to 2050Emissions an explicit objective; passenger acceptance and carrier mode choice both estimated; freight vehicles turn over by class, with load factors and empty running from NGM
Backcasting and pathways, not one forecast2050 targets defined on page 3; instrument orders searched backward from them
Methodological and practical contributionsThree testable claims and a named decision: revising the zero-emission discount and tariff

The gap. Strategic models give end states and NGM gives freight chains; neither carries acceptance. Norwegian agent work assigns traffic with MATSim but takes acceptance as given [tramodsim]. Le Pira, Marcucci and Gatta integrated discrete choice and agent-based models to evaluate the acceptability of urban freight policy [lepira]; their agents are stakeholder groups negotiating in rounds, not a population living through calendar time. Adaptive pathway methods sequence actions against tipping points [dapp, haasnoot] but treat acceptance as an external scenario. The deep-uncertainty frontier runs ensembles over transport agent models, most recently on a fictional city with acceptance left out [fuhrer]. The road-pricing acceptance evidence is careful and mostly static, and hybrid choice with a latent acceptance variable is now an established way to read it [hybridaccept, odeck08, borjesson16, toi2179]. Nobody has estimated acceptance on real data, carried it in agents over calendar time, and let it decide which passenger and freight pathways survive.

The question beneath the whole proposal is prior to any pathway: is public acceptance a measurable quantity that can be estimated on real data and carried forward in time, or not? The thesis answers that first; the ensemble and the robust front are what the answer is then used for, not the other way round.
1
Acceptance, estimated and carried, as an admissibility condition

First that acceptance can be estimated on real survey data and shown to persist (or not) between waves; then that a pathway counts only if that estimated acceptance stays above a threshold at every step, with the largest shift it survives reported as its acceptance margin — a result, not an assumption.

2
Uncertainty decomposed by source over a policy path

The spread in 2050 outcomes is split, year by year, into behavioural parameters, external futures and the choice of path, so planners see which uncertainty more data can reduce and which only adaptation can.

3
Signposts validated twice, and ordered across modes

Signals that a pathway is failing are scored on held-out futures for lead time and false alarms, then against dated events that happened; and the passenger and freight signposts are compared, because the slower fleet decides which fires first.

03 · THE MODEL

What each agent decides and remembers

What each agent decides and remembers. Each year t, a household or firm n chooses a vehicle, how often to cross and when, from a choice model where the instruments in force I(t) set the cost. Acceptance is estimated in its core, cross-sectional form in A1, as an integrated choice and latent-variable (ICLV) model on real wave-1 data, the hybrid-choice approach used to read acceptance surveys elsewhere [hybridaccept], extending Le Pira, Marcucci and Gatta from negotiating stakeholder groups to a population of individually estimated agents [lepira]. Acceptance depends on the dose actually paid, the information arm and covariates. Whether that latent construct is cleanly identified, and whether it persists, is the thesis’s first empirical test; the pathway machinery is built on its answer.

(1)  U(n,j,t) = β·cost(j, I(t)) + θ′·x(n,j) + ε(n,j,t)
(2)  A*(n,t) = ρ·A(n,t−1) + δ·dose(n,t) + η·info(n) + γ′·z(n) + u(n,t)
(3)  pathway p is admissible if the share with A* ≥ λ holds every year; its acceptance margin is the largest rise in λ for which p stays admissible.

The dynamic form (2) adds one first-order persistence term, identified between the two waves with the initial-conditions problem handled [wooldridge]. This ρ is a Level-3 extension, pursued only if both waves land; the core contribution does not rest on it. I claim only what the data identify: a cross-sectional acceptance model as the floor, one persistence term as the stretch, never a full dynamic panel.

Three agents over 2026–2050: the commuter crosses λ in 2031 and holds; the occasional crosser never leaves; the van driver, with the largest dose, falls below λ from 2035. ILLUSTRATIVE · ρ and dose shown are not estimates

What a pathway is, and how it is chosen. Five instruments: revision of the package, the zero-emission rate, a passenger distance charge, a heavy-vehicle distance charge, and earmarking of revenue. A3 is a search, not a catalogue: choose the switch-on year and level of each instrument to maximise the share of futures meeting all three 2050 targets and minimise maximum regret, subject to acceptance above threshold every year, revenue covering debt service, and an accessibility floor, with a many-objective robust algorithm over the ensemble and scenario discovery naming where the robust set still breaks [prim, mordm]. Treating robustness as the quantity to optimise follows the stability-metrics line of Shaabani, Hvattum, Hoff and Laporte [shaabani]. Full enumeration of a reduced set of four of the five instruments (ordered switch-on sequences, each later switch at one of three thresholds) is 4 + 36 + 216 + 648 = 904, kept to check the search; the full search ranges over switch-years and levels for all five, on the order of 10⁴ pathways.

Target in 2050MetricAnchor
EmissionsWell-to-wheel CO₂e from road traffic in the case areaClimate Change Act: 90–95% by 2050 [klimalov]
FinanceToll revenue ≥ debt service; failure if below three years runningPackage financing [innst337]
AccessibilityGeneralised cost of the lowest income quintile no higher than 2026Distributional floor, a design choice

What would falsify it. If ρ is near zero, agents need no memory and claim 1 reduces to a static result; if η is near zero, information does not move acceptance and H2 fails; if the fast engine cannot reproduce the network model within tolerance, the ensemble is cut to what the network model can run. Each is reported whichever way it falls.

Tools, and the honest skill path. Python throughout: Biogeme for estimation, the EMA Workbench for the ensemble and scenario discovery, OSMnx and NetworkX for networks, OR-Tools for routing checks, and NGM elasticities for the freight chains. My foundation is a logistics master from this faculty and an operations-research and programming background; I have not estimated choice models professionally, and I do not claim to. As a reproducibility check I estimated a standard mixed logit on the public Swissmetro data in Biogeme (N = 6,768, 1,000 Halton draws), reproducing the published normal-mixture reference (final log-likelihood −5214.9 against about −5214.8) [evdcm]. Choice-model estimation is the first named skill I deepen, in Year-1 coursework and under supervision in the Transport Research Group (TRG) at Molde University College.

04 · CASE AND DESIGN

Kristiansund, where acceptance is live

Why Kristiansund, and where freight enters. Bypakke Kristiansund began collection on 1 June 2026 at two rv70 stations, Nordsundbrua and Omsundbrua, in both directions; about 70% of the package is toll-financed over up to 15 years [bypakke, innst337]. A car pays NOK 34, 27.20 with a tag, 19.04 if zero-emission with a tag [vegamot]. The council approved the basis 26 to 19 and the county 33 to 14: acceptance here is contested and live. The town sits on the Møre og Romsdal west-coast corridor, where the Ferjefri E39 programme and NGM both treat coastal short-sea shipping as the competing mode for freight bound to Oslo and the continent [ngm]. Freight is estimated here, not borrowed: a short carrier stated-choice block gives the mode-and-timing response of hauliers to a distance charge, which the NGM chains carry to the network. Because the heavy fleet turns over slowly and the sea alternative needs volume to stay viable, a pathway that reaches road freight too late closes the modal-shift window and locks the emissions in. The thesis reports the year the freight signpost must fire, estimated from carrier behaviour; it is expected to fire before the passenger one, an expectation the design tests rather than a result it assumes. Molde, with no package, is the passenger comparison town.

Freight · acceptance live
The toll is not one price; it is a map of who can avoid it. Every building is assigned to the side of Nordsundbrua it reaches without the bridge (OSM graph). Red: Nordlandet, which only the bridge connects. Teal: the toll-free Atlanterhavstunnelen. Trip 1 pays at a station; trips 2 and 3 do not. REAL · OSM graph

Survey — three blocks, Bayesian D-efficient

Acceptance block (households): information randomised in three arms — personal cost as numbers, purpose as a short narrative, and control; the arms test format as well as content. Passenger stated-choice block: vehicle at next replacement, crossing frequency and time, under tariff and discount levels inside national ranges. Carrier stated-choice block (firms and hauliers): mode (road vs coastal short-sea), route and timing under a distance charge, single wave, small targeted sample — the estimated freight element, NGM-anchored. Kristiansund carries household and carrier design; Molde the acceptance block. Wave 1 and the carrier block in month 6; wave 2 in month 18 with the same households. Planning sample 1,428 households in Kristiansund, 714 in Molde, sized by minimum detectable effect.

Hypotheses

H1 acceptance persists once a charge is permanent (ρ > 0), tested as within-person change between waves against dose. H2 information moves acceptance independently of experience (η ≠ 0), tested by the randomised arms, turning the Norwegian correlation between information and attitude [odeck08] into a causal estimate. H3 (freight) a distance charge shifts carrier mode choice toward short-sea above a threshold rate, estimated from the carrier block.

Freight fallback

If the carrier sample under-powers, the freight arm reverts to NGM mode-split elasticities with a reported sensitivity on the key elasticity; the freight signpost is then a modelled consequence, and the thesis ladder absorbs it without loss of a complete dissertation.

05 · PLAN, ROBUSTNESS AND RECEIPTS

The robust front, and how it finishes in three years

The ensemble and the search, priced. The robust search explores on the order of 10⁴ candidate pathways, each scored against a Latin-hypercube sample of futures, with the surviving robust set re-checked on the full 10³ futures. Each evaluation advances a zonal state to 2050, about 25 ms, so the budget is roughly 40 to 150 CPU-hours, embarrassingly parallel and inside a desktop over a weekend. The fast engine’s fidelity is measured, not assumed: on the real OpenStreetMap graphs of Molde and Kristiansund it reproduces static-network car travel times per zone pair within about 15% mean absolute error (r 0.73 to 0.84) at three to four orders of magnitude less compute [evfid]. A dynamic cross-check against MATSim (Molde, 4,000 agents, 20 iterations) confirms the regime: at free flow the fast engine matches MATSim to about 19% (r 0.74) and the static assignment to 6% (r 0.999); under a tenfold capacity squeeze the free-flow engine breaks down, as such engines must, which is exactly why robust pathways are re-checked on the network model [evfid]. Passenger and freight vehicles carry class-specific load factors and empty running from NGM, which is what makes this a logistics question as well as a passenger one.

A thesis that survives a failed survey

Level 1, no new data: A1 on national ranges and A3 on NGM elasticities, freight included, are a thesis. Level 2, wave 1 + carrier block: adds H2, a cross-sectional A2, estimated freight (H3). Level 3, both waves: adds H1 and the dynamic persistence term, the stretch. Each level is a complete dissertation; the survey raises its ceiling. The guaranteed spine is my own collected survey, under my control.

Calendar

SSB and RVU microdata applications filed in week 1, off the critical path. Months 1–3: coursework incl. philosophy of science; Sikt notification; pilot with Norwegian-speaking co-authors. Month 6 wave 1 + carrier block · M14 A1 · M18 wave 2 · M26 A2 · M34 A3 · M34–36 summary. Articles are pipelined, not serial.

Why here. TRANSPLAN’s backcasting and its call for realistic, goal-directed plans [toi2172]; Molde’s strength in stated choice and transport economics and the DCM and ABM tradition in the TRG; and a Logistics programme where freight vehicle classes belong. Partners as possibilities: TØI for the national experiment’s ranges and NGM, CICERO for climate-policy acceptance, the Norwegian Computing Center for surrogate methods. Receipts. Every number traces to a tagged commit, with 89 automated tests, and figures are generated from the same code; code released openly, anonymised survey data deposited FAIR once Sikt allows; AI-tool use disclosed in the supplement. Dissemination. Three journal articles (A1–A3), a Norwegian-language piece in Samferdsel in year 3, and presentation at the annual NORS conference, where I have presented before.

→ The signpost that warns a path is failing is the same erosion page 1 showed already under way. The ring closes.
